### Bots go up Boneyard's sniper stairs: the wall check trusts the nav's next point, 2026-11-26

The owner's Boneyard bug report 20261126-200759: "My team on boneyard just likes to accumulate around the stairs below our teams sniper and they dont use the stairs properly. Just roam the bottom". Then: "I just seen bots not going up the stairs when they were completely able". Then: "Fix it but dont implement the one call per power weapon thing" (888100c reverted in 5c1cec3).

- **The match** (trace_reach_70_boneyard_20261126-200304): his bots stood at the stairs' foot (280, 112) 17% of their time on their half. 42% of that time their goal was upstairs: the rockets in the middle, the sniper, an objective, a hold. Of 318 tries from the foot, 9 went up. The rest shuffled there up to 11 s ("wall ahead: stepping around" 1,154 times, unstuck wiggles 644 times) until a hunt, retreat or fight took over.
- **Cause:** the way onto the stairs passes the corner of a block at (279.0-279.75, 111.5-112.0), walled from the floor to about 1.4 u. `Bot.redirect`'s chest ray (`Terrain.clearance`) reads that corner 0.25-0.5 u ahead, under `REDIRECT_D` 0.55, and turns the step 30 degrees aside. Its "a corner the nav turns at" exception only ran with the bot looking along its path (`att` "path"). These bots were watching the enemy. The nav's way up both flights is right (checked offline from each spot they stood on).
- **`brain/bot.py` `Bot.redirect`:** that exception also holds when this tick's step is the nav's own (`nav_cmd`) and the nav's next point (`s.wp`) is short of the wall hit (within its distance + 0.2 u), wherever the bot looks. A wall with the next point past it, or a step that is not the nav's, is stepped around as before. Every map and tier.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_stair_corner.py` (4 tests on Boneyard's level data, skipped without it: the corner reads as a wall there, the nav's step walks on, a step off the nav and a next point past the wall still step around). With the fix taken out, the walk-on test fails. Full suite: 1826 tests, with the same 2 `test_layout_lifts.py` failures as before. Import check of `brain/` and `tools/live_bots.py`. **Untested in game.**

### The Falcon's side guns hit: aimed from the gun, led for its round, 2026-11-25

The owner: "The falcon gunner never hits a shot. Dig and see if campaign aiming for ai is better than ours." Then: "DO all of them just no extra error per round", and, asked about Legendary's and Demon's protected aim: "Yes, this gun only".

- **What his matches showed** (Breakpoint 20261123-172845 and 20261125-175509; scratchpad `falcon/gun_shots.py`, `gun_hits.py`): 4,221 firing ticks on the side guns, with the man hurt after only about 9% of them. The gun was on him from the Falcon's middle (a median 0.2-0.45 deg off). The game reads every rider at the Falcon's origin, but each gun hangs on its door (HREK `falcon.render_model` marker `falcon_side_gun_left` on `b_hull`: 0.34 u back, 0.50 u out). The rounds a model aimed "dead on" hurt him less often (6-8%) than those it put 0.5-1 u off (11-20%): a steady offset. Its round (`falcon_machinegun_bullet.projectile`) flies at 100 u/s with no drop; it was led as the assault rifle's 324 u/s, and Legendary's and Demon's protected aim leads nothing. 56% of its firing ticks were at 20 u or more and a third past 30 u, where its 0.5-1 deg spread is wider than a man.
- **The campaign AI** on this gun (`generic.character`): combat range 4-12 u, 1.5 deg error a round, half the lead, 1.5-2 s bursts 0.75-1.25 s apart. Not more accurate: it fires from the real barrel and up close.
- **Aimed from the gun** (`vehicles.falcon_gun_origin`, `tools/live_bots.py`): each side gun's own mount (its object's parent-relative place, read like the Warthog chaingun's; else the model's -0.34, +/-0.50) at its height (0.38 u), as `turret_origin`.
- **Led at 100 u/s** (`vehicles.FALCON_GUN_SPEED`, `Aim.step`'s `shot_speed`), every tier. Legendary and Demon (the protected aim, lead 0) are locked on and led on this gun only (`Aim.lock`, as the Demon / Mythic chaingun, now with `shot_speed`). No extra error a round.
- **Trigger** (`Bot.falcon_gun_fire`): never on a man more than 30 u from the gun (`FALCON_GUN_MAX_FIRE`); the campaign's bursts, 1.5-2 s on, 0.75-1.25 s off (let go 0.75 s and the next press starts a new one).
- **Its pilot** holds 8-12 u (`FALCON_GUN_RANGE`; was 8-18), Reach only.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_falcon_side_gun.py` (11 tests). Full suite: 1793 tests, the 2 `test_layout_lifts.py` failures as before. **Untested in game:** that the live mount reads as expected, and whether its rounds carry the Falcon's own speed (the data leaned no).

### The brain no longer stops the first time a bot flies (air_hold), 2026-11-25

The owner's live Boneyard 20261125-170018: "Why is the game frozen?" The bots stood still from 92 s on. The brain stopped after 91 failed ticks ("TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'method' and 'float'", the first at 34.1 s).

- **Cause:** Nov 24's aircraft hold fire (ba18dd1) named its method `Bot.air_held`. That is already the name of the pilot's take-off clock `s.air_held`: `hold_for_crew` sets it, and `air_guard` reads it as `max(seat_since, getattr(s, "air_held", -1e9))`. A bot flying before it ever waited for crew got the method in that `max`, and every think pass failed. After a wait, the clock would also have replaced the method ("'float' object is not callable").
- **Fix:** the method is renamed `Bot.air_hold` (`brain/bot.py`: its def and its 4 callers; the comments in `brain/core.py`, `brain/profiles.py`, `tools/air_kills.py`, `tools/live_bots.py`). The take-off clock and the hold's behaviour are unchanged. `docs/AIRCRAFT_HOLD_FIRE_PLAN.md`, a plan of record, still says `air_held`.
- **Checks:** `tools/test_air_hold.py` 25 -> 26 tests (`PilotClock`: a new bot has no take-off clock, and `air_hold` can be called). Full suite: 1778 tests, with the same 2 `test_layout_lifts.py` failures as before. Import check of `brain/` and `tools/live_bots.py`. **Untested in game.**

### No getting onto a Mongoose with an enemy on radar, 2026-11-25

The owner, to "Also stop bots boarding a Mongoose while an enemy is on radar?": "Yes, add that".

- **`Bot.goose_off_limits`**, read at the start of every `decide`: an enemy it knows of within 25 m (8.2 u: `mongoose_radar`, the same test the dismount uses) and not exempt (`mongoose_exempt`: the objective in hand, a race). That tick `veh_banned` bans every Mongoose, so no path picks one: the director's ride / board / drive orders, a committed walk, a River errand, a Wheelman's pick, a trip's pick.

### Off a Mongoose when shot or with an enemy on radar, 2026-11-25

The owner: "We need a good rule for mongoose drivers dismounting while getting shot. Too many bots die while driving or riding on them. They dont do much. Maybe a rule like THey drive until an enemy is on radar, or as soon as they get shot and dismount?" His picks: hit or radar, driver and passenger, every tier and game; a flag or objective carrier and racers ride on.

- **What his matches showed** (Forge World, 20261125-002025 and -003335; scratchpad `goose_deaths.py`): 39 of 259 bot deaths on a Mongoose (33 + 6) for 20 kills from one; drivers 20 deaths for 7 kills, passengers 9 for 7. Killed by DMRs 14, melee from a man beside them 8, frags 3, the Warthog chaingun 3, falls 3, Warthog splatters 2. In the fatal rides an enemy came within 25 m a median 5 s, and the first hit a median 4.5 s, before the death.
- **`Bot.mongoose_bail`, every tick on a Mongoose (`Bot.drive`), driver or passenger:** off (Use held, as every get-out) the moment it is hit since it got on (the perception's `hurt_at`), or an enemy it knows of, in view or a tracker dot no more than 1 s old, is within `MONGOOSE_RADAR_R` (Reach's motion tracker, 25 m = 8.2 u, flat). Its trip ends as a finished one does: on foot, no vehicle for `MONGOOSE_RETRY` (30 s), a drive / ferry / ride order freed. Note: "mongoose: shot, off and on foot" / "an enemy on radar".
- **Not:** with the flag, the ball or Invasion's core; in a race; any other vehicle (the Gungoose included).
- **Replaces** a Mongoose driver's drive away from a man close by (`evade`) whenever he is within 8.2 u: it gets off instead.
- **How often it fires** (the same traces, true positions, scratchpad `goose_cut.py`): on 52 of 73 rides in the first match (27 of those ended in death), a median 10 s in; on 9 of 34 in the second. Trips will often end short of where they were going.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_mongoose_bail.py` (7 tests); `tools/test_mongoose_transport.py`'s evade check changed to the dismount. Full suite: 1773 tests, the 2 `test_layout_lifts.py` failures as before (this machine's level data). **Untested in game.**

### Revenant, Scorpion and Falcon: the owner's picks from the campaign AI, 2026-11-24

The owner, after a comparison of the campaign's Falcon, Scorpion and Revenant with ours (HREK `tags\ai\generic.character` and the vehicles' own tags, read only): the Revenant's minimum range, shorter range and its arc worked out from its shot; the Scorpion's feet aim "in all scenarios it can see their feet. Other wise shoot at the chest", its turn throttle, "Change running down boarders to just prioritizing them first and foremost over anything else within a range", its pathfinding footprint; the Falcon flying where its side guns can reach the man, "along side our code". His picks: every tier but Easy, Reach only; boarders within 10 u, the tank holding still; the tank ground widened to 1.75 u; the computed arc past 20 u only.

- **Revenant** (Reach, at the wheel; `Bot.drive`, `vehicles.driver_view`):
  - **Holds 7-15 u** (`REVENANT_RANGE`, the campaign gun's normal combat range); it held 10-30 u. Other games keep 10-30 u.
  - **No shot inside 4 u or past 25 u** (`REVENANT_MIN_FIRE`, `REVENANT_MAX_FIRE`: the gun's minimum and maximum firing range). Its own splash inside 4 u.
  - **Its lob past 20 u is worked out from its shot** (`vehicles.revenant_lob`): 16 u/s slowing to 8 over the first 20 u of flight (the projectile tag; the reading of its "acceleration range" is inferred), and a gravity fitted so the lob at 20 u is the measured 9 deg, where the owner's measured lob (0.6 deg a unit, capped at 9, 75 shots at 10-20 u) still applies. 13 deg at 25 u. The tag's own gravity (0.33 of ours) gave only 4.7 deg at 20 u, so it is not used.
- **Scorpion** (Reach, at the wheel, every tier but Easy):
  - **His feet when the shell's line from the camera reaches them, else his chest** (`Bot.scorpion_sees_feet`, the level data's shot line). This replaces fixed Legendary and Demon's chest aim at every man on foot (Nov 8), on the owner's word; their turn cap and settled shots are unchanged. Where there is no level data: his feet.
  - **A man on foot within 10 u (`TANK_FOOT_R`) is its target first, the nearest of them, whatever their scores** (`Bot.vehicle_pick`), **and it holds still to shell him**. It no longer runs a boarder down (Nov 20). A man in Armor Lock is backed away from as before. The Wraith keeps its run-down and scores.
  - **Its turns:** throttle never under 0.6 on its way (it dropped to 0.35 on sharp turns), and its view leads a turn by as much again as it is off, the extra capped at 0.5 rad and never past 1 rad off its hull (Bungie's oversteering scale 2). Other games, Easy and the other tanks as before.
  - **Its ground is 1.75 u clear of walls** (`Terrain.VEH_ROOM_TANK` 5 -> 7 cells; Bungie's pathfinding radius 1.8 u). The Wraith and Mantis share this ground. As `brain/terrain.py` is part of the terrain cache's key, each map's next match builds its terrain once again.
- **Falcon** (Reach pilot in a fight, `Bot.falcon_gun_height`): its fighting height is moved only as far as needed so the man is inside its side guns' pitch, 60 deg down to 25 deg up (the side gun's seat in `falcon_side_gun_left.vehicle`), 5 deg inside it: up when he is above, down when he is too steeply under. Its other height rules (`air_guard`, the floor clearance) still apply afterwards.
- **Not ported:** Bungie's slowed AI shots, damage cuts, burst gaps and 4-6 s between Scorpion shells (they make its AI fair to lose to), its engine pathfinding (we have no equivalent of driving over obstacles).
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_campaign_vehicles.py` (13 tests); `tools/test_vehicle_gun_reach.py`'s run-down test changed to the hold. Full suite: 1766 tests, 2 failures in `test_layout_lifts.py` (the cage), which fail with the old tank width too: they read this machine's level data. **Untested in game.**

- **`brain/director.py` mode_slots:** the haven markers and the hot spots are one pool, shuffled once a match (`surv_pool`, the director's own random), so a group's spot is any of them; the spots stay put for the match. Rooms with few ways in still come after the pool, and the last 3 still take a room with one way in.

### Infection survivors in groups of 3 at most, each at its own spot; the last 2-3 in a room with one way in, 2026-11-24
The owner, live Anchor 9 Infection with 18 players (trace_reach_dlc_slayer_20261124-215447): "all the bots are standing in one hold. I think it should do a check of how many people are there and if its like 4 or more survivors find a new spot. Or even use the hot spots on the map in the survivors logic"; "Plain. And make it to where if there is only 2-3 survivors left they try to find and area with only 1 entrance".
- **Cause:** Anchor 9 has 9 Infection haven markers. With any markers on a map, every survivor went to the one nearest the team as if it were Safe Havens' active haven (all 15 bots' orders at about (0, 17) all match); the rooms logic only ran on maps without markers.
- **Now (`brain/director.py` mode_slots, `brain/modes.py` `survivor_spots`, `last_stand_hold`, `SURV_GROUP` 3, `SURV_LAST` 3):** plain Infection's survivors split into groups of 3 at most (a 4th starts a new spot), people standing within 4 u of a spot counted in its 3; each group's spot at least 12 u from the others' (closer if the map has too few). The spots: the map's haven markers first, then its hot spots (positions.json), then rooms with the fewest ways in (find_holds). 3 or fewer survivors left: all hold the nearest room with a single way in (else the fewest). The roles are handed out again every pass, so a group that grows past 3 sends the extra on. A survivor wanders at most 1 u from its spot at every Infection post (`brain/bot.py`), not only on maps without markers.
- **On Anchor 9's own data:** 15 survivors take 5 spots, 3 each, three at haven markers ((0, 17), (-8, 2), (6, 3)) and two more ((-12, 17), (12, 14)); 3 left take the room at (-0.4, 20.1), one of its 2 rooms with one way in.
- **Validation:** new `tools/test_infection_spots.py` (5); full suite 1753 tests, 2 failures in `test_layout_lifts.py` (Forge man cannon and lift throws) that fail the same without this change. **Untested in game.**

### Bots hold fire on an enemy Banshee or Falcon until it has killed enough of their team, 2026-11-24

The owner: "banshees dont get mutilated at once, but also theyre not flying freely". Demon, Mythic and Noble shoot its crew at once. The rest wait for the aircraft to kill their team: Legendary 1, Heroic 2, Normal 3, Easy 5. His answers: "Yes, in self-defence"; "Blind can be heroic level for this"; "Noble will be counted the same as a demon"; the count resets "When the banshee is destroyed"; "Add the Falcon"; "Only on foot"; people's deaths count ("Yes"); "Leave the sim alone", "That means no switch"; built "live only (B)". Design: `docs/AIRCRAFT_HOLD_FIRE_DESIGN.md`, plan: `docs/AIRCRAFT_HOLD_FIRE_PLAN.md`.

- **Each difficulty's number (`brain/profiles.py` `air_hold_kills`):** Demon, Mythic, Noble 0; Legendary 1; Heroic, Tactician, Blind 2; Normal 3; Easy 5. Scaling 0: it plays as before (Scaling stays out of fixed-tier rules).
- **The hold (`brain/bot.py` `Bot.air_held`, `air_hold_scores`; `AIR_HOLD_KINDS`, `AIR_SELF_DEFENCE_S` 3.0):** a bot on foot leaves everyone aboard an enemy Banshee or Falcon (its pilot, a Falcon's gunners) out of `pick_target`, patrol targets, its fight scores and the Grenadier's vehicle hunt (`enemy_vehicle`) while that aircraft has killed fewer of its team than its number. It keeps fighting everyone else. Within 3 s of a hit from anyone aboard, it shoots back. Bots in any seat keep today's anti-air rules. With no count (`Snapshot.air_kills` None: every sim and test), nothing changes.
  - `decide`: `t` is None when everyone in view is held crew. The fight-commitment block then keeps its goal (and `air_hold_scores` drops it if held), never `("fight", None)`.
- **The count (new `tools/air_kills.py` `AirKills`; `tools/live_bots.py`):** `{aircraft handle: {victim's team: kills}}`, handed to the bots each pass as `snap.air_kills` (`air_table`). None in free for all, where there is no team count to wait on.
  - Reach: the game's own kill record (`kill_record.Watch`) now runs in every Reach match, recorded or not. It writes its rows to the recording only when there is one. Each row that reads as a kill (not a betrayal, suicide or after the match) by a man aboard a Banshee or Falcon counts, people's deaths too. The killer's seat comes from this pass, else the last one (a trade). A Falcon gunner already reads as riding the Falcon.
  - With no kill record (other games, or the record switched off after read failures): a bot's death as `events()` credits it (bots only, a guess). Never both at once.
  - An aircraft that reads destroyed or leaves the vehicle list is dropped: its count starts again at 0.
  - The map memory (`book.add_kill`) still takes kills from recorded matches only, as before.
- **Not changed:** `tools/real_sim.py`, `tools/banshee_sim.py` and their goals; pilots' flying; bots in vehicles.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_air_hold.py` (25 tests: each difficulty, Scaling, the counter, people's deaths, betrayals, trades, the reset, the hold, self-defence, in-vehicle bots, `pick_target`, `decide` with only held crew in view, the fallback, free for all). `unittest discover` over `tools`: 1748 OK. Import check of `brain/` and `tools/live_bots.py`; `kill_record.py` self-check OK. **Untested in game.**

### No learned shoot-through holes in solid walls (Boneyard), 2026-11-24

The owner's bug report `20261124-194946` (Boneyard, t 157): "Bots are trying to shoot through boneyards walls"; asked, "Fired rounds into it"; then "As long as it only blocks small holes and not the larger holes in railing and stuff".

- **What it was:**
  - He stood behind a solid wall at about (273-275, 109.5-110.25). Camper25, 40 u off, fired 10 rounds in a row at PacMan behind the same wall (148.5-152.6 s); none landed.
  - The variant's `walls_learned.json` (spots the bots learned rounds pass, `Terrain.learn_shot_through`) had 7 cells at the foot of that wall. With them the bots' line read clear on 135 of 141 ticks; without them, on 3.
  - The file was full (300 of `SHOT_MAX` 300), so nothing new could be learned there.
  - Nov 9's rule (no learning where the wall runs from 0.6 u under the line to 1.2 u over it) missed the foot of a wall, where the floor is nearer than 0.6 u. It also read the walls with earlier learned cells already opened.
- **`brain/terrain.py` `Terrain.solid_run` / `solid_slot`:** a height is inside a solid wall when the level's own wall (`level_walls`) runs unbroken from 1.2 u over it down to 0.6 u under it, or down to the floor it stands on. `learn_shot_through` learns none there.
  - A railing, grate or sill stops short of 1.2 u over the line, and a gap in a wall breaks the run, so their holes are learned and kept as before.
- **`brain/maps.py` `_build`:** learned cells that are such holes are dropped when the map loads, from use and from the file at its next save, freeing their places under the 300. Each load prints how many it dropped.
  - Of the files with a terrain cache here: Boneyard 30 of 300, Settlement 89 of 403, Aftship 44 of 172, Launch Station 36 of 139, Condemned 7 of 23, Ivory Tower 5 of 35, Prisoner 4 of 15, Panopticon 3 of 102, Beaver Creek 2 of 21, Park 1 of 30, an Asylum variant 1 of 47, the rest 0.
  - On his Boneyard line, 4 of the 7 go and the line reads clear on 12 of 141 ticks. The other 3 sit where the level's data has a gap in the wall over the line, so they stay.
  - Every learned file is backed up first, in `logs/backup_walls_learned_20261124` (not in Git).
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_learn_solid_wall.py` (5 tests: a floor-standing wall learns nothing, and learned it without the rule; a railing and a wall with a gap still learn; the file rule). `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK on both Pythons (1723 tests), and so is the `live_bots` import. **Untested in game.**

### Reach's Wraith driven like the campaign's, 2026-11-24

The owner: "Can you delve into the campaign files and see how the ai drive wraiths?", then "Yes, match Bungie". His picks: every tier but Easy, Reach only, turtling = stop and keep firing, our mortar's rate of fire kept.

- **Where Bungie's numbers are (read only):** HREK's `tags\ai\generic.character` ("vehicle properties", wraith: stationary fight (tanks), the charge, turtling), its `wraith_mortar` weapon row (normal combat range 8-16 u, 4-50 u), `objects\vehicles\covenant\wraith\ai\wraith.style` (the behaviours it may run) and `wraith.vehicle`, exported with `tool.exe export-tag-to-xml`. The campaign scripts (`data\levels\solo\*\scripts`) only point its mortar (`cs_shoot_point`) and send it to places; the engine's AI drives.
- **`Bot.reach_wraith_fight` (Reach's Wraith at the wheel, Normal and up):**
  - **Fights from a stop** from 8 to 16 u, and closer between charges; drives in from farther. It had held 15-40 u, strafing all the while, and backed off anyone within 6 u.
  - **Charges** a man or vehicle inside 8 u at where he will be in 1.25 s; given up past 10 u, on a miss (him more than 0.25 rad off its nose inside 3 u) or after 6 s (ours); the next one 10 s after.
  - **Turtles** (`reach_wraith_turtle`): its body down 20% within 3 s (the window is ours; the tag gives none), it holds still and keeps firing for 5 s, a fresh hit keeping it on up to 10 s. Read from the snapshot's `left`.
  - **No mortar inside 4 u**, the campaign mortar's minimum firing range.

### A bot's first round after dropping the bomb comes when the gun is ready, 2026-11-24

The owner: "So in the last match around the 5-minute mark, I previewed how fast you can shoot after you drop the bomb. I did it 3 different times. Record it and apply it to the bots."

- **His measure** (Condemned Neutral Bomb, `20261124-185819`, his data collector): three drops at 418, 422 and 428 s on the brain's clock, about seven minutes in. His DMR was in hand the tick each drop was read, and its first round left (the magazine read one less) **0.57, 0.71 and 0.57 s** after the drop.
- **The bots in that match:** of their drops to fight that fired, the first round came 0.67–2.69 s after, about 1.05 s typically.
  - Some pressed 0.07–0.1 s after the drop: the press was lost to the gun not being ready, its fire gap charged, and the first round still came about 1 s in.
  - Others pressed only 0.9–2.7 s after.
- **Fix (`brain/bot.py` `drop_ready_wait`, `DROP_READY_S` 0.57, `DROP_RETRY_S` 0.5; `flag_fight_phase` notes the drop):**
  - Until 0.57 s after a drop to fight, the trigger stays up and the bot's aim stays on the man.
  - At 0.57 s, the press on that very tick, then the press-and-release retry the grenade throws use (`retry_after_grenade`) until the magazine shows the round, without a lost press charging the fire gap.
  - This covers every drop to fight: One Bomb and Neutral Bomb, and CTF and Stockpile flags. A flag's drop is the same game action; only the bomb's was measured.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_drop_ready.py` (4: no press before the gun is ready; the press at the ready tick, then a release and a fresh press; dead or carrying again, no wait; his measure). `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK on both Pythons, and so is the `live_bots` import. **Untested in a match.**

### Version numbers: Project Noble's own X.Y.Z (0.0.325 today), the update check ranks it above the old releases, 2026-11-24

Upstream 0.3.0's note #67 (build 20261119-0733, his "build numbers are back", 0.2.3 s-191 from BUILD_NO). The owner: "the owner's own scheme, X.Y.Z. Z = commits on GitHub (wraps to 0 past 1000, and Y goes up one); X counts releases from the next one (next release = 1, then 2...), and the old 4 don't count; at a release Y.Z keep the all-time GitHub commit count (e.g. 1.0.340). Today = 0.0.325". His BUILD_NO and build_name are not used.

- `tools/noble_version.py` (new): `from_counts(commits, releases)` gives `X.Y.Z` (Y = commits // 1000, Z = commits % 1000). In a Git checkout: commits = `git rev-list --count origin/main` (GitHub's main as last fetched; else the branch's `@{upstream}`), X = the highest X of the `vX.Y.Z` tags with X >= 1 (`v0.2.2-custom.*` and the checkpoint tag do not count). In an installed copy: the `NOBLE_VERSION` file. `next_release()`: X one past the last release tag, Y.Z HEAD's commit count, tag `v<version>`. `python -I tools/noble_version.py` prints both.
- `tools/updater.py`: `current()` is the scheme's version (kept a minute: the page asks every 2-3 s), else CUSTOM_VERSION (an older install still reads its own), else VERSION. `version_key()` now starts with the scheme: a plain X.Y.Z with X >= 1 (or 0.0.Z before the first release) is scheme 1, everything before (upstream's 0.2.2-s181 and plain 0.1.0 to 0.3.0, our 0.2.2-custom.N) scheme 0, so every new version is newer than every old one. A dev copy at 0.0.325 is not offered the old 0.2.2-custom.14 release; an install at 0.2.2-custom.14 is offered 1.0.x (its own older updater reads 1.0.x as newer too). Limit: a copy reaching 1000 commits before the first release (0.1.Z) would read as old again. The update check still reads only our GitHub releases (`RELEASES` unchanged). `current()` closes its file now.
- `tools/build_installer.py`: the release version is `next_release()` (printed with its tag at the start; a note when no release tags are fetched), stamped into the payload's `NOBLE_VERSION`, and it names the Setup (`ProjectProvingGrounds-Setup-<version>.exe`) and its AppVersion. CUSTOM_VERSION is no longer the release's version.
- The launcher shows it where it showed CUSTOM_VERSION ("Version 0.0.325"), through `version()` / `updater.current()`.
- `docs/CUSTOM_RELEASE_WORKFLOW.md`: a Version numbers section; releases titled `Project Noble <version>`, tagged `v<version>`. `CUSTOMIZATIONS.md`: the version sentence.
- **The next release's tag:** `v1.0.<commits of the released commit>`, e.g. `v1.0.340`. Today this branch's HEAD would build as 1.0.409 (325 on GitHub plus this branch's commits), and that grows with every commit until the release. No tag or release was made.
- **Checks:** `tools/test_noble_version.py` (new, 15) OK: the wrap at 1000 and the owner's example; only new-scheme tags count; a stamped copy; this checkout's own count (0.0.325); a dev copy not offered v0.2.2-custom.14, older installs offered v1.0.340, comparisons between new versions, the old comparisons and `updater.selftest()`, upstream plain versions stay old, old notes are no news; the updater's API is our repository; current() prefers the stamp, an older install reads CUSTOM_VERSION, the answer is kept; the build stamps the payload. `tools/test_launcher_noble.py` OK. Setup not built.

### No freeze on vehicle maps when new drives come in: the car and tank grounds are rebuilt in the background, 2026-11-24

Upstream 0.3.0's note #40 (build 20261119-0039), **our own version from his idea, not his code**. The owner: "our own version for car and tank grounds, measured on Boneyard and Spire". His single vehicle ground would have dropped our separate car and tank grounds and our wedge marks (Nov 13).

- `brain/terrain.py` (ours):
  - `_vreset` (new rides, paint, out of bounds): with `VNAV_LATER` on, each size that has a ground keeps it, marked stale (`_vstale`), instead of dropping it for a rebuild in the pass.
  - `_vready` (`vnav`, `drive_clear`): a size never built is still built in the pass, as before. A stale one starts its rebuild (`_vfresh`, `_vbuild_job`) on a thread of its own, from a shallow copy of the terrain taken then, and bots drive on the old ground meanwhile.
  - The new ground goes in whole under `VLOCK`. The other size's result goes to its store for its next drive (`use_vground`).
- **Both sizes:** each keeps its own graph, room rule (`VEH_ROOM` / `VEH_ROOM_TANK`) and caches.
  - One rebuild at a time per terrain, so never two of one size; the other size waits for its own next drive.
  - Rides that come in again during a rebuild mark it stale again, so it is rebuilt once more after.
- **Wedge marks:** the copy gets its own lists. A mark made while the ground was built (`vwedge`) goes onto the new ground before it goes in (and onto the old one at once, as before). Per-size marks and `vwedge_nodes` are unchanged.
- **Think threads:**
  - On: a rebuild done during a threaded pass goes in at the next pass (`_PASS["seq"]`), so every bot of a pass drives on one ground whichever thread asked first.
  - Off (one thread, the live brain on our bundled Python): at the next drive.
  - A grown nav swapped in meanwhile (`maps.swap`): the rebuild is dropped.
  - No thread or job is kept on the terrain itself (`_VJOBS`, weak), so the terrain cache still pickles.
- `VNAV_LATER` is off by default, so the sims and tests play as before (a drive after a change builds in the pass, the same every run); `tools/live_bots.py` turns it on. `tools/test_threads.py` (4 threads play the 1-thread match) still passes.
- Not taken of his: `_VNAV`, `_vnav_stale`, `_rebuild_vnav_later` and his `vnav` / `add_rides` / `oob` lines (one ground, no wedge marks).
- **Measured** (`reach_70_boneyard/variants/v8d2f4510` and Spire `reach_35_island/variants/v704f87f3`). Their own `rides.json` came in again through `add_rides`, 3 times each, with 240 passes of 6 car and 4 tank drives and their guards' looks, at 30 a second:

  | | In the pass (before) | Off the pass (now) |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Boneyard, worst pass after new rides | 674, 676, 679 ms | 72, 99, 95 ms |
  | Spire, worst pass after new rides | 525, 529, 529 ms | 79, 80, 67 ms |
  | Calm pass (median) | 15 / 12 ms | 15 / 12 ms |

  - New grounds in use after about 0.5 s (car) and 1.1 s (tank) on Boneyard, 0.3 s and 0.6 s on Spire.
  - The worst passes left are the fresh route fields on the new ground and the build sharing Python's lock.
  - `add_rides` itself is unchanged (56-74 ms on Boneyard, 14-19 ms on Spire).
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_vnav_later.py` (7) OK, 6 runs in a row:
  - off, the next drive builds in the pass as before;
  - the old ground is driven on until the new one goes in whole, once;
  - both sizes, one rebuild at a time, each into its own place;
  - a wedge marked while it is built is on the new ground;
  - threaded passes take it at the next pass;
  - a grown terrain swapped in meanwhile drops it;
  - a terrain with a rebuild under way pickles.

  `test_tank_drive.py`, `test_threads.py` and the full suite OK; `live_bots.py` imports. **Untested in a live match.**

  - **Else a weighted pick:** the file's weight, times up to 1 + `LANE_W` (3) for the territory short of its share of the team (down to `LANE_MIN` 0.25 for one with twice its share), times `ENEMY_SPAWN_W` (0.25) by the other side's spawn, and 0 with a seen enemy within `DANGER_R` (15 u).   - `label_zone` uses `label_pick` live, kept per death and phase, and sets the errand for a ride.

### More of every map used: your hot spots count, stale spots pull, Flanker crossfires, Rushers push, high ground, 2026-11-24

The owner: "bots dont use alot of space on the map. Like Boneyard rocket building is a stronghold in game but barely is ever used. Banshee building isnt utilized enough. They all just stay outside in mid", "I usually place hot spots where I want bots of high caliber to go, but even then it doesnt seem to affect them a ton", and "Rushes should always just use sneak paths or flanks and push the entire time". Then: "Build 1,2,3,4,5 all in one phase".

Measured first, from his last two Boneyard 8v8 Slayer matches (`20261120-164229`, `20261124-003150`, both before today's Take Space change):
- Bots on foot were on the ground 87% of the time and in Mid 46–49%.
- The east building (rockets, Spartan Laser, sniper, the neutral Banshee) got 0.0–0.2%.
- The bots can walk there from mid and both bases.
- The owner's 5 marked spots (of 13) got 43% of the Slayer post weight, against 38% unmarked: score 1.0 over the computed spots' 0.7–0.95.

The changes:
1. **Your hot spots count.**
   - `Director.post_weights`: Slayer posts weigh the owner's own hot spots ×3.5 (`OWNER_POST_W`). On Boneyard that's 72% of the post weight, before the hot zone's ×2 for spots that see the fight.
   - Take Space (`Bot.space_pick`) counts them 15 u nearer for Legendary and up (`OWN_SPOT_HIGH`, `profiles.fixed_high`). Other difficulties keep 6 u.
2. **Team map coverage.** `Director.coverage_tick` records when one of the team (bot or person) last stood within 6 u of each power position (`cover_seen`, handed to the bots). A spot nobody has stood on for 60 s is fully stale.
   - Slayer posts weigh a stale spot up to ×2 (`COVER_POST_W`).
   - The sweep goes to a power position by those weights 60% of the time (`SWEEP_SPOT`), and otherwise anywhere as before.
   - Take Space counts a stale spot up to 8 u nearer (`SPACE_STALE`), for everyone using it.
3. **Flanker crossfires.** A Flanker's Take Space can also take a spot to the side of the fight that sees it, no more than 5 u farther from it (`CROSS_BACK`).
   - It counts a spot up to 20 u nearer the farther round the fight it is from every teammate, in full at 75° (`CROSS_BONUS`, `CROSS_FULL`).
   - It weighs the fight's distance 0.15, not 0.3 (`CROSS_TARGET_K`).
4. **Rushers push.**
   - They're out of always-on Take Space (`SPACE_ALWAYS` is Flankers only).
   - Every trip of theirs over 15 u to the fight or the objective goes round by a side zone (`Bot.detour`). Easy's still runs straight.
   - In CTF they always take a sneak route when the map has one (`RUSHER_SNEAK` in `pick_route`).
5. **High ground.** Legendary and up count a Take Space spot up to 4 u nearer for its height over its surroundings (`HIGH_SPOT`, full at 5 u).

Fights, hunts, recharges, power weapon calls and grabs, power vehicle jobs and objective jobs still come first.

- **Validation:**
  - `tools/test_map_use.py` (11 new): coverage and staleness; post weights; Boneyard's owner share 65–75%; Rushers no longer always on; the owner's spot for Legendary vs Heroic; a stale spot's pull; high ground for Legendary and up only; Flanker crossfires and side spots (and not without a line to the fight, nor for others); Rushers' detours; the CTF sneak route.
  - `tools/test_take_space.py`: Rushers are now in the list of styles that aren't always on.
  - Full suite: 1,483 tests OK; `live_bots` imports.
  - **Simulation:** Boneyard's variant, 8v8 Slayer in `tools/real_sim.py` (the real brain), 3 seeds × 6 minutes, the same tiers on both teams. Bots on foot, sampled every 0.5 s, with these rules off → on:
    - on a hot spot: 9.5% → 13.4%;
    - on one of the owner's: 4.3% → 6.2%;
    - high ground (z > -7.5): 18.2% → 19.0%;
    - the east building: 11.5% → 9.7%;
    - the mid strip: 47.0% → 50.1%.
  - **What the simulation shows:** the bots use hot spots about 40% more, but no more of the east building. Three of the owner's five Boneyard spots are in the mid strip, so weighing them more pulls bots there, and one computed east spot (297, 90.8, -4) can't be reached.
  - **The simulation's limits:** it doesn't reproduce live's 0–0.2% in the east (it has no weapon pickups and no vehicles but the Banshee). Three seeds are noisy: the east share was 7–13% per seed.
  - **Untested in a live match.**

  |---|---|---|

### The bots think on several cores (upstream 0.3.0's threads, ported), 2026-11-23

The owner, after reading the upstream author's 0.3.0 release ("the bots split their thinking over several cores"), unpacked from its installer without installing it: "Yes, download it", then "Yes, start the port".

- **The free-threaded Python:** Astral's python-build-standalone `cpython-3.14.10+20261026-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc-freethreaded-install_only` (the release's SHA-256 checked) in `E:\Proving Grounds\python314t`, outside the project, with numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1 and Pillow 12.3.0 (our versions).
  - The whole brain and tools load on it with Python's lock off, and every test passes on it.
  - On one thread it is about 10% slower than our Python (Renegade benchmark 26.7 / 73.0 ms against 24.1 / 67.0).
- **New `brain/threads.py` (`Pass`)**, adapted from upstream's (its notice kept): every bot's think of a pass on a pool of threads, on what the pass started with. What one bot's think would change for the others is held back and applied after the pass, in the players' order:
  - the Terrain's learning;
  - our team tables (`TEAM_SIGHTINGS`, `TEAM_EYES`, `TEAM_FACING`, `TEAM_TARGETS`, `TEAM_CRACKED`, `TEAM_ATTACKERS`, `TEAM_SPACE`, `BOT_PROFILES`, `DEAD_SPOTS`) and the map's vehicle duds;
  - Noble's hit book and habits, and the lore's jumps.

  A bot reads the pass's start plus its own writes (one more than upstream's: its own claim holds within its think).
- **Made safe for threads:**
  - **`brain/terrain.py`:**
    - the route-field caches are locked, and a field from before a learned wall is not kept (`gen`);
    - a route with one-off costs runs on a copy of the graph;
    - the optional tactics' search budget is per thread (`opt_state`); a field another thread kept this pass counts as fresh to it (`fresh_to_me`), so the budget doesn't depend on which thread got there first;
    - the vehicle ground, whose car and tank graphs swap in on use, takes one route at a time (`VLOCK`, `vlocked`; `brain/bot.py` holds it round its `vroomy` reads);
    - the hazard memo reads once.
  - **`tools/field_pool.py`:** a lock; a think thread never waits on a helper (`no_wait`).
- **The rule (upstream's): a threaded pass plays the one-thread match.** New `tools/test_threads.py`: 8 against 8 on Hang 'Em High, 240 ticks, every man's place, facing, shield, health and life the same on 4 threads as on 1.
  - Checked longer by hand: 600 ticks on 1, 4 and 6 threads all the same.
  - The old serial loop, without the held-back writes, plays another match from tick 17, so the test can tell.
- **Live (`tools/live_bots.py`):**
  - The thinks run through `Pass` (`think_job`; each bot finished in the players' order after: `finish_bot`).
  - The thread count (`think_threads`): `PPG_THINK_THREADS`, else Auto, half the PC's threads, 2 to 6, never past its threads less one, and none while Python's lock is on. The owner's PC (16 threads): 6.
  - `tools/play.py` `brain_python` starts the brain on the free-threaded Python where it is (`PPG_BRAIN_PYTHON` names another; `PPG_THINK_THREADS=0` keeps ours).
  - The simulator takes a `Pass` too (`tools/banshee_sim.py` `think_pass`); `tools/bench_brain.py --threads N`.
- **Measured** (60 simulated seconds of 8v8, the thinks' wall time per pass, median / slowest tenth):

  | Threads | Renegade | Utopie |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 27.8 / 68.1 ms | 23.4 / 98.5 ms |
  | 2 | 17.8 / 51.9 ms | 12.9 / 78.0 ms |
  | 4 | 9.7 / 46.9 ms | 7.9 / 72.2 ms |
  | 6 | 7.9 / 45.3 ms | 6.8 / 73.2 ms |

  The slowest passes wait on one bot's long think, which threads can't split.
- **Checks:**
  - New `tools/test_threads.py` and `tools/test_think_threads.py` (the count, the brain's Python).
  - `tools/test_route_cap.py` reads the per-thread budget.
  - `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK on both Pythons (1452 tests), and so is the `live_bots` import.
  - **Untested in a match.**

I think they shouldnt ban runners anymore", and "On that map its just a little rock jump up thats below the flag on blue side they get hung up on. But their is plenty of routes to their flag".

- **The cause:**
  - Three runners stood 2–8 u from their flag, still on its stand, from 345 to 385 s, waiting for a defender to look away ("peek") and for their shields.
  - `Bot.headway` saw 6 s with no progress and banned the flag for 30 s as unreachable. "Another spot by the objective" stood in at 0.7–0.98, and guns lying under the stand (2.1, a 16 u way back up) beat it.
  - The flag was reachable (6 u by route), and the team carried it at other times. A loose objective was already never banned; one on its stand was.
- **Fix (`brain/bot.py` `runner_objective`, `reroute`, `reroute_hazards`; `headway`; the bans in `decide`; `think`):**
  - A runner's objective (its order's point) is never banned.
  - A stalled way marks the spot it stalled at: its next waypoint, 2 u round (`REROUTE_R`). That spot is a hazard to its route for 30 s (`REROUTE_S`), the last 3 of them (`REROUTE_MAX`), kept while the objective is the same: `Terrain.nav` treats it as a wall while any other way exists, and goes through it when there is none.
  - A runner's side trips (a gun it can't reach) are still dropped, so it can't loop on one.
- **On Renegade:** from where a runner stood under the blue flag, its way of 14.6 became 22.0 round the stall, and from under the stand 16.2 became 28.1. The next step turned away from the rock jump.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_runner_reroute.py` (5: a stalled runner reroutes, not bans; spots add up to 3, then expire; a new objective drops them; others still give up, and a runner's side trip too; `runner_objective`). `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK, and so is the `live_bots` import. **Untested in a match.**

### A Forge layout's nav cut to its play area (Renegade), 2026-11-23

The owner, on Renegade's nav (`reach_forge_halo/variants/vf1ed8bb6`, the 8v8 CTF layout): "Remove the waste from renegade and see what you can do".

- **The waste:**
  - Its nav was 3,463,608 points: its window (130 × 277 u at 0.25 u, 6 floor levels).
  - 315,544 of them were reachable, and 176,381 of those were out of bounds. Forge World's ground goes on past its kill zones, and kill zones are only a cost on the nav, so every full search still walked them.
  - The window only ever grew: the union of every match's, and grown whenever a player came within 8 u of its edge.
- **Fix (`brain/variants.py` `play_window_of`, `play_limit`, `clip`, `save_play_window`; `brain/maps.py` `load_map`, `grow`; new `tools/play_window.py`):**
  - A layout's play area is the floor a player reaches inside its kill and safe zones, 6 u round it, on a 4 u grid. It is kept in its `variant.json` with a fingerprint of its `killzones.json`.
  - Its nav window is cut to the play area and never grows past it.
  - A layout whose kill zones changed is the whole window again until `tools/play_window.py` is run on it.
  - A grown window saved never shrinks the kept one (`save_window`: the union).
- **Renegade, worked out:** its window (−128, −256, 32, 32) became the play window (−100, −224, 0, −52), 37% of the area.
  - It kept all 98 in-bounds spawns, both flag stands and every in-bounds post. Lost: one power position out of bounds at (6.9, −11.9).
  - The nav went from 3.46 to 1.62 million points (6 levels still: its stacked floors are in bounds). Reachable went from 315,544 to 155,618, with 139,163 in bounds both before and after.
  - A full route search went from 28.1 to 16.2 ms, and the build from 11 to 8 s.
  - The 15-bot route test went from 86.5 to 65.5 ms a pass on the brain's thread alone, and from 33.7 to 24.9 ms with the helpers.
  - (The play window is in the layout's folder, `maps/…/variants/`, which is not in Git.)
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_play_window.py` (4: kept and used while the kill zones are the same, dropped when they change; no limit, no cut; a grown cut window never shrinks the kept one; growth stops at the play area). `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK, and so is the `live_bots` import. **Untested in a match.** Other Forge layouts are unchanged until `tools/play_window.py` is run on them.

### Route searches on helper processes; the fixed targets' routes kept all match; the brain at above-normal priority, 2026-11-23

The owner, on giving the bots room in 8v8 without changing their play: "Do 1 and 4 through completion. And then 3 afterwards". Python's threads take turns: 8 route searches on 8 threads ran 1.1× faster. So:

- **4. Priority (`tools/live_bots.py` `raise_priority`):** the brain's process is at Windows' above-normal priority, not high, so the game is never starved. It needed the 64-bit pseudo handle; with a plain `int` Windows refused.
- **1. The route-search helpers (new `tools/field_pool.py` `Pool`; hooks in `brain/terrain.py` `_field`):**
  - **The helpers:** three helper processes (numpy and scipy only) work out route fields on other cores. Each holds a copy of the nav's graphs in shared memory, never the brain's own: the brain changes weights in place for a moment (a carrier's risky edges). A lasting weight change clears the walking fields (`FieldCache.gen`), and the graphs are published again (5 ms on the 8v8 layout). A result of an older graph is dropped.
  - **Results:** they land in shared-memory slots (24), read in place with no copy. A slot read in the last 0.5 s is not used again.
  - **`_field` asks the pool first:**
    - a finished field goes into the cache;
    - one in the works is waited for (80 ms at most);
    - otherwise a cached field of the same search for a goal within 1.5 u (the same floor) stands in while the exact one is worked out, so a chase never waits for its moving target's field.
  - **Asked ahead (`prefetch_routes`, `Terrain.prefetch`):** each pass, the fields each bot on foot will likely walk (its goal's point, the man it fights or hunts, its order's point) are asked for before the bots think.
  - **A helper gone:** the searches are the brain's again, as before.
  - **Measured on the 8v8 Forge World layout** (15 walkers, two thirds chasing a moving man, 40 passes): the brain's thread spent 33.7 ms a pass on routes instead of 86.5. 570 of 600 next steps were the same; the other 30 walked by a stand-in at most 1.5 u off for a pass or two. Sharing the nav at the match's start takes 38 ms.
- **3. The fixed targets' routes (`Terrain.pin_targets`, `fixed_targets`, `Pool.pin`):** the flag stands and returns, the objectives' goals and zones, the hill, the power positions and the reachable power items.
  - The helpers work them out at the match's start (13 on that layout in 0.63 s) and they are kept all match, apart from the cache's turnover, up to 600 MB.
  - They are worked out again when the nav's weights change. A search cut short (`field_from`) is in them too.
  - **On that layout:** 180 walks to six of them took 39 ms instead of 710, the next step the same in all 180.
  - Not built after the match as first proposed: with the helpers, they take under a second at the start, and need no disk.
- **Checks:**
  - New `tools/test_field_pool.py` (6: the helpers' field is the brain's, a limited one; a weight change taken; a stand-in near, none far or of another search; a fixed target kept and redone on a weight change; a helper gone).
  - `tools/test_think_half.py` +1 (`fixed_targets`).
  - `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK, and so is the `live_bots` import.
  - **Untested in a match:** the next profile shows the passes. `brain/terrain.py` changed, so the next match's terrain is built afresh (its cache key).

### Bots with nothing on think every other pass, 2026-11-23

The owner, on the bots thinking every pass in 8v8, fighters first: "Yes, do it".

- **`tools/live_bots.py` (`THINK_HALF`, `full_rate`):** the bots think one after another, so a pass is all fifteen thinks added up.
  - A bot with nothing on now thinks every other pass, half of them on each pass. Its last command stands in between, since botcore applies a slot's last command every game tick until the next one, so a press lasts one pass longer at most.
  - Its next think's time step is its own since it last thought (up to twice `MAX_DT`). A bot never sits out two passes running, nor once its last think is 2 × `MAX_DT` old.
- **Who thinks every pass:**
  - anyone in a vehicle or on a vehicle job, or carrying;
  - anyone fighting;
  - anyone with a jump, lift or cannon ride under way;
  - anyone hurt in the last 2 s, or with an enemy seen or on radar in the last 3 s (an angle held, a corner);
  - anyone whose last think hit an edge, a wall, a step, a jump, a corner or a grenade.
- **In the owner's last 8v8 CTF** (`20261123-190955`), by the recording (which lacks the bots' radar), about a quarter of the bots' passes would have been sat out: some 12% less thinking.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_think_half.py` (5: a plain walk, fighting, driving and carrying, an enemy known lately, hurt lately, at an edge or a jump). `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK, and so is the `live_bots` import. The pass loop's skipping is not unit-tested. **Untested in a match.**

### Walking routes searched only as far as the walker, 2026-11-23

The owner, after another 8v8 CTF on that Forge World layout (`20261123-190955`, with the profile fixes): "The bots play really bad in 8v8 and idk why, Almost unplayable", and "Bug reports also show cosmic playing slow" ("Comis toook too long to shoot back", 192.9 s). His Task Manager showed 25–31% CPU: the brain runs on one of the PC's 16 threads, so at full load it shows only about 6% of the total.

- **What the profile showed:**
  - The passes were down from 194 ms to 153 ms (median), with 37% still over 100 ms.
  - Full route fields (`Terrain._field`, the whole layout's 3.46 million nodes, 33 ms each) were 47% of the slow passes.
  - Cosmic, a Demon, thought slowest of the 15: 33 ms a pass on average, 86 ms at the 90th percentile. Every Demon and Mythic was in the top five.
  - The bots think one after another each pass, so one pass is all fifteen thinks added up, and each bot's aim gets a new command once a pass.
- **Fix (`brain/terrain.py` `field_from`, used by `Terrain.nav` and `Bot.headway`):** a walk's field is searched out from its goal only as far as the walker needs: twice the straight way plus 20 u, for trips under 50 u. When the walker lies past that, or for a longer trip, it is the whole map's, as before.

  - On that layout, 60 of 60 next steps were the same, and a fresh one took 12.7 ms instead of 31.9 ms.
  - A search out to 40 u takes 5 ms against 33 ms for the whole layout.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_field_from.py` (3: the short search, past its reach the whole map, a long trip). `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK, and so is the `live_bots` import. **Untested in a match:** the next profile shows the passes.

### The brain's profile in every match, 2026-11-23

The owner, after an 8v8 CTF on a new Forge World layout (`20261123-182210`) where the brain's passes took 194 ms (median; 15–35 ms in the day's other matches) and the bots played badly: "Yes, profile first" (before spreading the bots across cores).

- **New `tools/brain_sampler.py` (`Sampler`):** a thread looks at the brain's main thread every 10 ms and counts the function it is in (self time) and every function on its stack (total time).
  - The counts are kept for the whole match and, apart, for slow passes (a pass already 100 ms long when sampled).
  - It uses `time.sleep`, not `Event.wait`: on Windows a wait wakes on the 15.6 ms system tick.
- **`tools/live_bots.py`:**
  - It starts the sampler before the first tick, and each pass sets its start.
  - The report, `logs/brain_profile_<map>_<stamp>.txt` (the trace's stamp), is written every 60 s and when the brain stops. It lists the top 40 functions by total and by self time, and the 25 commonest stacks of brain and tools frames.
- **Overhead:** 0.8% on route searches and sight checks on that layout's nav (none measurable in a second run). It never stops the bots: any error in it is caught.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_brain_sampler.py` (2 tests: a slow part found in the slow passes, the report written; no thread, no error). `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK (1408 tests), and so is the `live_bots` import. **Not yet run in a match**; its first report comes with the next one.

### Reach Banshee pilot: it can see the men it dives on, and its trigger is the bomb only, 2026-11-23

The owner, live Spire (bug report 20261123-173345, "Bot wont shoot in banshee"): "Had a ton of great angles and good shot opprutunities. Its flying well, its just not shooting", then "I dont care about the plasma cannons. I want them to only use the bomb".

- `brain/terrain.py`: the shooter's-floor rule is skipped when the shooter is more than `NO_FLOOR_H` = 1.5 u over the floor under it (`height_over`). The target's-floor rule is unchanged, so a man on the ground still has no line to an aircraft steeply over him (the earlier two-way fix lost kills in the sim and was reverted).
- `brain/bot.py` (`think`): a Reach Banshee pilot's trigger goes out only as its bomb's shot (`fuel_rod`, the bomb selected); its cannons never fire.
- Validation: the same recording replayed against the map's check: 1020 of those 1318 positions now read in sight and with a round's line (15-45 degrees unchanged, 186 of 340). Full suite 1395 OK; `brain.bot` and `brain.terrain` import. `tools/banshee_sim.py`, Boneyard seeds 1-5 (with the uncommitted sticky target too): 6, 13, 4, 6, 7 Banshee kills, mean 7.2, no gain there over the last batch's 7.3; "no clear line" 0-6 rows a game, 10-25 bomb shots a game. **Untested in game.**

### Theater plays your films through MCC's own Theater, and walks MCC there, 2026-11-23

The owner: "Start making all of the other menus that arent Matchmaking work accordingly". Asked, he chose the full way (like Custom Game: the pick set in MCC's own screen, started by MCC's own start), Theater first, and no bots in these modes for now.

- **What MCC does (static read with Ghidra of the Oct 31 2026 MCC-Win64-Shipping.exe; addresses in `native/theater.cpp`'s head):**
  - MCC's screen registry names "Theatre". Its screen (vtable `0x143296FB0`) has its film list at `+0x920`, each film's 16-byte content id at the item's `+0x2A0`, and the chosen film's id at `+0xFF4`.
  - `FUN_14035B3EC(screen)` is its START FILM. It finds the film in the content library `[0x1440016C0]` (kind 2, films), sets the launch up for theater and asks MCC's UI to launch.
- **botcore (`native/theater.cpp`, new; `theater_hooks` from `session_watch.cpp`; in `build.bat`):**
  - It hooks the Theatre screen's Update (`FUN_14035B0E0`, MCC's UI thread). While MCC's Theater is open, it reads MCC's film list when the screen opens or the list changes.
  - Each film is matched to its file on disk by the file's name or its header's unique id (`_blf` chdr, 8 bytes at `0x60`) somewhere in MCC's library entry. Which of the two works is not known yet. The first reading is written to `native\bin\theater_library.txt` with three entries dumped, as the evidence for the next step.
  - START FILM puts the film's id into the screen and calls MCC's own START FILM, unless MCC is already counting down. The screen closing within 10 s counts as started.
  - The byte heads of every function it calls are checked first. With any other MCC build it stays off and says so.
- **Project Noble's THEATER lobby (`native/proving_grounds_reach.inc` `rm_theater`, `rm_film`; page `RP_FILM`):**
  - **CHOOSE FILM** lists this PC's films (Temporary History and Local Files, as the File Browser reads them), newest first. Each row shows its map and its time; the focused film's game, map, date and recorder are at the right. MCC's map keys show as map names.
  - **START FILM** plays the chosen film in MCC's Theater. Project Noble closes once MCC leaves its Theater.
  - Until MCC's Theater is open it says "Open Halo: Reach's Theater in MCC first: the film plays there". Walking MCC there by itself waits for the route to Reach's Theater from MCC's main menu.
  - The film files' header ids are now kept by the File Browser's scan (`fb_file.uid`).
- **Preview:** case 50 (`reach_choose_film`); case 42 with `PG_LOBBY=3` shows the lobby; `PG_TH_LIVE=1` shows it as if MCC's Theater were open.
- **First live run (botcore_pg58, the owner, 3:43 PM):** it worked. MCC's 12 films were read, START FILM went to MCC's own, MCC's Theater closed and loaded the chosen film (`asq_mglo-6_45_launch_9AD58628_6B0494FA.mov` opened, the launcher's `boot.log`), and Project Noble closed.
  - `theater_library.txt` showed 0 matches only because MCC's Theater was read before Project Noble's lobby handed over the files. The next reading matched, since START FILM needs a match.
  - MCC's library entry holds the film's whole path (a text record at `+0x1F8`), so the file-name match is the one that works. The file is now written on the first reading that has the files.
- **MCC walked to its Theater (the owner recorded the route; botcore_pg59):**
  - From MCC's main menu it is Down, Down, A, Down, A, then `Theatre.gfx` opens (`boot.log`).
  - `native/menu_route.cpp` now has a second route, `MR_THEATER`: out with B and to the top with Up as before, then those five presses 1.5 s apart, until `Theatre.gfx` opens and MCC's Theatre screen runs.
  - `overlay.cpp` starts it once each time Theater's pages are opened (`pg_wants_theater`) while MCC's Theater is not open. Project Noble stays drawn while MCC leaves Reach's lobby under it.
  - The custom game lobby's screens see a Theater route only while it runs (`lobby_route`), so a stopped one never blocks a search.
  - The lobby says "Opening Halo: Reach's Theater..." and then "Reading MCC's Theater...". START FILM pressed meanwhile goes once the film is listed.
- **Checks:** `build.bat pg59` builds `botcore_pg59.dll`, and the preview builds.
- **Live (pg59, the owner, 3:50 PM):** the walk worked, with all 12 films matched and the film loaded, but the owner said "it takes quite a while". In `boot.log`, `Theatre.gfx` opened about 20 s after the Theater lobby: 13 s of B ×8 (0.9 s apart) and Up ×10 (0.5 s apart), then 6 s of his five presses at 1.5 s. MCC itself then takes about 5 s from START FILM to its loading screen, as it did when he pressed it by hand.

### Reach One Bomb / Neutral Bomb: the attackers' team pushes, and the clock kept after round 1, 2026-11-23

The owner: "I want the bots on attack to notice when there is 15 seconds or less on the game clock and if it hits zero they lose. But sudden death starts if youre holding the bomb when the game clock hits zero ... Also I want teams to notice when 3-4 players are dead on defense and the team director does a push order ... Or when the bomb is within 3-5u of the plant site, have everyone urgently push/fight to plant it". Then: "We dont do multi bomb so make it neutral and one bomb. and yes do 75%".

- **Team pushes (`brain/director.py` `Director.bomb_push`, called first in `desperate`):** these apply on Reach maps in Neutral Bomb and One Bomb (`Bot.single_bomb`), for the attacking team only (the one with a goal to plant on), and only while the bomb isn't armed. Each push runs through the team blitz.
  - **Our bomb within 5 u (flat) of its goal:** everyone goes to the goal ("bomb: at the plant site").
  - **Our bomb with 15 s or less on the clock:** everyone goes to the goal with it ("bomb: the last seconds"). At 0 it becomes "bomb: sudden death".
  - **The bomb loose with 15 s or less (or at 0):** everyone goes for it, so someone holds it when the clock runs out ("bomb: the last seconds, take it"). A defender holding it in One Bomb is no push.
  - **75% or more of the defenders dead (3 of 4):** everyone goes in, to the goal with our bomb or to the loose bomb ("bomb: their defense is down").
  - The carrier isn't in the blitz team, so he keeps the plant-first rule. Defenders' play is unchanged.
- **The push goes at once (`blitz_tick`):**
  - A `bomb:` push never gathers at a rally point and never waits out the 15 s cool-down, so "the last seconds" turning into "at the plant site" carries straight on.
  - Assault's sudden death counts as overtime (`overtime`), as Invasion's does: no time limit and no pause between pushes.
- **The clock after round 1 (`tools/live_bots.py` `match_sane`):**
  - In the owner's One Bomb game on Launch Station (`trace_reach_45_launch_station_20261123-142103`), from round 2 the game kept team 0's score in the upper half of the word ({0: 65536, 1: 0}).
  - `match_sane` threw that read away whole, the clock with it ("match read dropped"), so the bots had no clock for the match's last 6 minutes.
  - Now a score whose upper half is a score is read from it. Garbage scores drop only the scores, and the clock and limit are kept.
- **The replay of that match (the drop rule, Nov 18):** it was active, with 3 drops ("flag: dropping it to fight") and the carriers going back for the bomb. Most carrier deaths were too quick for it: from 1.25-2.0 health to dead within one quarter-second read. About 4 of the 11 were round resets, with the enemy 140 u away. The rule drops only when the damage would empty him within 1.5 s, so it rarely had the chance. Left as it was.
- **Checks:** new `tools/test_bomb_push.py` (15 tests: each push, its limits, defending, armed, non-Reach maps, two-bomb Assault, One Bomb, sudden death as overtime, the immediate go, no cool-down). `tools/test_land_grab.py` has the 65536 read and keeps the clock with garbage scores. `unittest discover` over `tools` is OK (1392 tests), and so is the `live_bots` import. **Untested in a match.**

### Skill ratings in place of the team points, and Reach's RATING page, 2026-11-23

The owner, with a screenshot of Reach's carnage report RATING page: "do calculations similar to my already standing balance system I have in place, but use the rating system reach did". Then: "the teams would balance by total skill rating per team", and his numbers, agreed one question at a time. His +2/−1 team points are gone.

- **The rules (`native/skill_rating.cpp` / `.h`, new):**
  - **Bots:** each bot has its own rating, saved by name. A new bot starts at a random spot in its difficulty's range: Easy 400 (300–500), Normal 600 (500–700), Heroic 800 (700–900), Tactician 950 (850–1100), Legendary and Blind 1300 (1150–1450), Mythic 1600 (1500–1700), Demon 1650 (1550–1800), Noble 1700 (1600–1800). Scaling isn't in his matchmaking and borrows Legendary's.
    - A win is +19, or +9 for beating a team whose average is more than 150 lower.
    - A loss is −19, or −9 for losing to a team averaging more than 150 higher.
    - No kill bonus, and a bot never leaves its range.
  - **People:** the player and each friend who joins have their own rating, starting at 1600, never under 1500.
    - A win is a random +35 to +40, including when beating a stronger team. Beating a team more than 150 lower gives +30 to +35.
    - A win adds up to +3 more for kills above the lobby's average (1 per 3 over), never minus.
    - A loss is −15, or −10 for losing to a team more than 150 higher.
    - Quitting gives +15, so the next teams are tougher, and nothing else.
  - **Other matches:** a draw changes nothing, a bot that quits takes a loss, and Firefight isn't rated.
  - **Free for all** has its own rating: 1st +40, 2nd +30, 3rd +20, the rest −15.
  - **Storage:** everything is kept in `native\bin\pg_ratings.txt`, with the last match counted. The first time, the match already played is marked counted, so it isn't rated.
- **The balancer (`native/bots_panel.cpp`):**
  - A seat now counts its bot's rating instead of its difficulty's points. A person counts 1600, the player and each friend their own, on the teams they were given.
  - Clans, pinned parties, every split tried, and the 60/40 Demons stacked or spread rule are unchanged.
  - Splits within 50 (`SR_TIE`) of the most even one count as even. Ratings rarely tie, so without this the 60/40 rule would have nothing to choose from. The owner's 8v8 test lobby is within 50 every time, with Demons stacked in 1188 of 2000 deals, as before.
  - The lobby shows each team's total rating. The pool help text and the Balance teams tooltip say ratings.
  - `bot_pool_set_person_points` became `bot_pool_set_people_ratings`. `tier_points` and `HB_HUMAN_POINTS` are gone.
- **Project Noble (`native/proving_grounds.cpp`, `proving_grounds_reach.inc`):**
  - **When a match is rated:** each match `last_match.txt` reports is rated from `last_carnage.txt`, the same way as before (once a second, and at once when the carnage report opens). A game too short to count is never rated.
  - **Bot difficulties:** each bot is rated at the difficulty it was seated at. Its saved one is used next, else Legendary.
  - **Redealing:** the waiting lobby is dealt again after a match.
  - **RATING page:** the carnage report's second Stats page (now Page x/7) shows each player's rating after the match, in score order, with no comma, like Reach's.
  - **Psych Profile:** TEAM POINTS is now SKILL RATING. It shows the player's team and free-for-all ratings, and A resets both to 1600.
  - **`win_points=`** is no longer read.
  - **Preview hooks:** `PG_CG_PAGE` and `PG_FOCUS` pick one Stats page or Psych Profile row in the preview. The preview rates in memory only.
- **`tools/service_record.py` `write_last_carnage`:** each player line ends with whether they finished (MCC's `mCompletedGame`, 0 if they quit). Older files without the column read as finished.
- **Builds:** `skill_rating.cpp` is in `build.bat`, `build_pg_preview.bat` and `build_pool_test.bat`. The pool test build also lacked `armory.cpp`, which since Nov 19 left it unable to link; that's fixed too.
- **Checks:**
  - `native\build_pool_test.bat`: all pool checks pass. The new section 27 covers bases and ranges, starts, close wins and losses, the 150 gap both ways, the kill bonus, quitting, a draw, the floor and ranges, Firefight, free for all kept apart, reading back from the file, the reset, and the friends' ratings in a dealt lobby.

### Sim-vs-live scorecard; the game's read delays in banshee_sim, 2026-11-23
The task: make the offline match simulator trustworthy by measuring it against the owner's real Asylum matches, then add the game's real delays to it. The owner: "Use most of my data from the asylum games", "All games on ayslum to count".
- **`tools/sim_scorecard.py` (new):** one parser for live traces and for sim runs (the sim's recorder writes rows in the live trace's shape). It reports DMR accuracy by range (<3, 3-6, 6-12, 12+ u) and by the target's sideways speed (<0.5, 0.5-1.5, >1.5 u/s); for kills, the time from the first hit, the kill distance and how often the first hitter won; and alive time by goal, plus retreating with the shield down. With no `--live`, it reads every trace in logs/ played on Asylum (`v8e4a8930`): 29 matches from Nov 20-23, every mode and tier, one trace at a time. `--sim N [--delay]` runs 4 Demon vs 4 Noble Team Slayer DMR on Asylum; `--show` prints saved runs side by side; `--delays` prints Noble's measured delay spread. A round is the bot's DMR magazine dropping. A hit is the target's shield + health lower in the next world row (rows are about 0.27 s apart). Several shooters on one target can each be credited with the same hit, so 4v4 rates read a little high.
- **`tools/banshee_sim.py`, `Match(delay=True)` / `--delay` (off by default):** each bot thinks on its own read of the game, `DELAY_Q` old in whole 60 Hz ticks. `DELAY_Q` is Noble's logged lead over all 29 Asylum matches (390,248 rows): median 26 ms, 90th percentile 88 ms. `vel` (the move since that bot's last read x 30), `vel_t` (the move over the game time between its reads; a read of the same tick keeps the last) and `read_wall` are set the way `tools/live_bots.py` sets them, so `Bot.noble_lead_s` and `lead_ray` run as live. The action and the shot land on the tick's present world; directors read the present. `tools/real_sim.py` (cd43357) already calls `Match(delay=...)`; this commit brings that code into Git.
- **Live vs sim (3 sim games each, 12 minutes, to 50):**
  - DMR hit rate at bots: Demon live 70%, sim 43%, with delays 39%. Noble live 74%, sim 38%, with delays 37%.
  - At 12+ u: live 71-73%, sim 30-33%. Against a target moving over 1.5 u/s sideways: live Demon 68% / Noble 75%; sim 42% / 41%; with delays 38% / 35%.
  - Time to kill from the first hit, median: live 1.5 s, sim 3.2 s, with delays 4.2 s. First hitter won: live 84%, sim 85%, with delays 89%.
  - Retreating, share of alive time: live Demon 25% / Noble 30%; sim 44% / 49%; with delays 43% / 54%.
- **What it says:** live accuracy hardly changes with range or the target's speed; the sim's falls from about 60% under 3 u to 30% past 12 u. The sim's hit model (hitscan along the view, a 0.2 u body and a 0.09 u head, no aim assist or bullet magnetism) is the biggest gap. The delays are real but cannot match live until hits do, so they stay off by default. Of the later steps named (bloom, magazines and reloads, sprint, grenades, jetpack, a ghost of the owner's movement), none closes this gap, and bloom would widen it. The next step is Reach's aim assist and magnetism with the real hit volumes. The slow kills explain the extra retreating time.
- **Validation:** `tools/test_sim_scorecard.py` (8 tests: rounds, hits, bands, first hitter, goal shares; delay sampling and ticks, the delayed read with its vel / vel_t, a same-tick read, `noble_lead_s` reading the age, `lead_ray` on `vel_t`); full suite OK; `live_bots` imports. Live code untouched: the delay model runs only in the simulator.

### The once-a-minute LiDAR save in its own process: no more freeze on the minute, 2026-11-22
After the route cap (701057b), the owner's 22:37 and 22:44 Asylum matches still had thinks of 260-670 ms, every one on the minute (60.6, 120.5, 180.6, 240.8, 300.8 s ...). The owner: "Alright try to fix it"; asked first, "I dont want to lose any kind of edge".
- **Cause:** `tools/live_bots.py` saves the people's LiDAR once a minute, merging into maps/<map>/lidar.json (Asylum's: 3.1 MB, about 100,000 walked cells read, merged, sorted, written): 420-445 ms, timed on a copy. It ran on a thread, but Python runs one thread at a time: a think's every numpy call let go of the lock and the save took it, so the think lasted the save's length. Reproduced on a copy of the file: a 22 ms think made of numpy calls took 462 ms during the save. The jump check (5 ms), the rides save (1 ms) and `save_learned` (under 1 ms) are not the cost.
- **Fix (`tools/lidar_saver.py`, new):** `merge_save` is the merge and write `Recorder.save` did, moved unchanged; `Recorder.save_payload` (`tools/lidar.py`) is its first half, what is new since the last save. `Saver` starts a helper process (the same Python, no window, below normal priority, the standard library only) at the first save and keeps it for the match; live_bots hands it each minute's payload and it merges and writes the file. At the match's end the last save is waited for and the helper exits (`close`). Any failure (no start, a crash, no reply in `REPLY_S` 60 s) stops the helper and saves in the bots' process as before; the next save starts a new one. LiDAR mode, the simulator and every other caller save in place as before. Still saved every minute; the file is the same.
- **Measured on a copy of Asylum's file:** HEAD's save, the new save in place and the helper wrote byte-identical files (3,173,307 bytes). During the save the 22 ms numpy think's slowest run: 462 ms (HEAD), 432 ms (in place), 47 ms (the helper: the payload's copy). The bots' brain and play are unchanged.
- **Validation:** new `tools/test_lidar_saver.py` (4: the merge keeps what the old save kept, the helper writes the same file over two saves, a broken helper saves in place, nothing new is not added twice); full suite 1350 OK. **Untested in game.**

### Sight and shots pass over a Forge piece's real top; no blind return fire, 2026-11-22
From the owner's Asylum match (3 Demons vs 4 Nobles, logs/trace_reach_forge_halo_20261122-195647) and his theater screenshots: CactusMailbox at 00:25 ("he shot 2 in 2 an a half seconds while seeing me the entire time"), "I was never out of its sight line once", GravyCompass at 4:27 ("shoots at me through the ground twice, then doesnt shoot me against when it can fully see me"), and "If I can see any part of a spartan as long as its not through a glass wall, I can shoot them. Either by seeing their legs, or only their head".
- **Cause:** wall heights are stored in 0.25 u steps (`wall_bin`). A placed piece's wall face (`Terrain._face_walls`) fills the whole step its top reaches, so a face topping out at 61.33 stood to 61.5. GravyCompass, below the owner's Forge platform, had its line to his head blocked at 61.46. CactusMailbox's lines read blocked at 14.3-14.6 s and from 15.3 s, by a lip and a pillar. Sword Base has no Forge pieces, which is why this did not show there on Nov 20: trimming every wall one step cleared 1 of its 8 wrongly blocked kill lines, against 18 of Asylum's 54.
- **Fix (`brain/terrain.py`):** `_face_walls` keeps each cell's exact highest wall point of a piece (`piece_top`) and a copy of the level's own walls before any piece (`level_walls`). In `_ray` (sight and shots), a wall bin hit more than `PIECE_TOP_EPS` (0.03 u) over that cell's piece top is no wall, unless the level's own walls are there too. Walking and the nav are unchanged. The terrain cache rebuilds (its key covers terrain.py).
- **Measured on the three Asylum matches today:** real kill lines the model calls blocked: 54 of 289 -> 42 (making every wall one step shorter would reach 36, but would open real walls too). CactusMailbox at 14.3-16.1 s: the owner's head and chest clear at every moment, where only a shoulder or nothing was before (before 14.3 s, a natural rock lip, untouched). GravyCompass: his head clear at 253.9-254.3 s; the rest of its lines cross the platform's edge 0.3 u under its top, still blocked.
- **Return fire (`on_sight_fire`):** today's rule that shot back at a man who hit it in the last second, whatever the line check said, sent GravyCompass's two rounds into the platform's edge at 251.7 and 252.2 s (the owner's "through the ground"). Removed: the man hitting it is still looked at, his line checked like anyone's.
- **Validation:** new `tools/test_piece_top_los.py` (3); `test_on_sight_fire.py`'s return-fire case now expects a line; full suite 1331 OK. **Untested in game.**

### Noble shoots any part of a Spartan's outline it sees, 2026-11-22
The owner: "I want to make the Noble bots able to shoot at any part of the spartans model it sees. Legs, feet, head,Chest, shoulders"; "Even add like the sides tops of the heads"; "The entire outline of the spartan should be shootable".

Its lock aims there, led by the read's age (`lead_ray`). The fire-tick snap in `think` goes to it, and `fire_gate` takes the press. Noble only; Demon and the rest unchanged.

### Shoot on sight; reloads wait while a man is near, 2026-11-22
From the owner's Asylum match with his friend (logs/trace_reach_forge_halo_20261122-190403): "Bots are reloading as soon as they get a kill with over more than half a mag of dmr ammo", "when an enemy peaks I want the bot to instantly shoot them at whatever body part they see no matter what", "at the 1:27 mark gravy compass stales to kill bbaventures. Then flicks over to ChlShade and losses a gunfight", "theyre reloading with ammo in the mag when people are shooting them and are on radar", "At 1:59 cactus mailbox ... when repeeking didnt shoot instanly even with a visual".
- **1:27 (73.0-74.1 s):** GravyCompass (Mythic) had its aim on the owner's friend at 13.6 u for 1.1 s with no press. Its goal was BBAdventures, one shot from dead ("one shot" callout) and out of its line. The friend shot first and won.
- **1:59 (108.0-108.9 s):** CactusMailbox (Demon) backed onto a ledge losing the odds. Its view stayed on the friend within 0.5 degrees, but every line its map checks (feet to head) was blocked. The friend's one shot from below killed it: the game had a line, its map did not.
- **New `Bot.on_sight_fire`** (Legendary, Blind, Tactician, Mythic, Demon, Noble), run before `fire_gate`. With no press this tick, if the view the game has now passes within 0.22 u of a part of an enemy in its eyes (head down to the legs), in reach, with a line to that part, it presses at its gun's pace (`fire_gap`, a release between presses), whatever it plans. The shot's part is what it sees: the head, else the chest (`shot_part`, so Demon's and Noble's snaps go there), else where the view is. A man who hit it in the last 1.0 s (`ON_SIGHT_HIT_S`) is shot without the map's line check, since his rounds prove the line. No press with a charge, splash or blade gun, an empty magazine, sprint, a held armor lock, a throw or a melee. `fire_gate` takes its press with that man's line (or his hits).
- **Reloads (`reload_check`):** in that match 110 of 122 DMR reloads had 8+ rounds of 15, an enemy within 25 u at all but one, and half came within 3 s of a hit. In 31 the man came into its sights before the magazine refilled (the "stall to shoot again"). Now, with a man known within 30 u in the last 3 s (eyes, radar, heard, a callout; dead men left out) or a hit in the last 3 s, it reloads only at 25% or less. Within 4 s of a kill, at 50% or less. The 80% top-off is kept for quiet moments. An enemy's armor lock (`Kit.fight_move`): it backs off and reloads only at 50% or less.
- **Tests:** `test_reload_timing.py`'s hit case now expects the 3 s wait. `test_shoot_back.py`'s on-the-way scenes test that rule with on_sight_fire off (their man stands dead ahead of the view, which on_sight_fire now shoots).
- **Validation:** new `tools/test_on_sight_fire.py` (9); full suite 1316 OK. A 2-minute 4 Noble vs 4 Demon Asylum sim ran clean: 161 of 378 rounds pressed by on_sight_fire, no top-off reload (a man always near in a 4v4 there: bots now fire down to 3 rounds). **Untested in game.**

### Bots no longer run to weapon spawns the game type never fills, 2026-11-22
The owner's report "Why arent they killing me" (Asylum, TU TEAM SLAYER DMR, logs/bug_reports/reach_forge_halo_20261122-155713: at 269.8 s all four enemy Demons had one goal, an "item" at (52.4, 223.2)) and his question "how did they have two empty weapon spots, They have ars and dmrs?".
- **Cause:** the layout's .mvar places two snipers (52.4, 223.2 and 73.3, 203.4; 90 s) and two shotguns, which the DMR game type never spawns. `tools/live_bots.py item_check` starts a spawn's timer when a bot comes within 25 u of it and nothing lies there ("taken, or not in this game type"). When the timer ran out the spawn was still empty, so the timer started again. Each time it came due, `director.power_runs` sent a Demon onto the empty sniper spot ("power weapon run: committed", 2,419 notes), and each bot's own `best_item` read the same timers. The four enemies spent 2,273 trace rows, about 9% of their time, on those two spots.

A gun lying there again sets it back to up, as does a gun back on time, so its next take is timed anew. A real power weapon taken by an enemy is timed as before.
